# DAHÄM HTTP API

The Java service (`dahaem-api`) is the engine behind the PHP frontend. It is **internal only**: no published port,
reachable at `http://dahaem-api:8080` on the Docker network. Everything below is JSON over HTTP and lives under
`/api`. This page is generated from the controllers and DTO records (`scripts/docs/generate_docs.py`); the javadoc of
each controller method is the source of the descriptions.

## Calling it

| | PHP frontend (production) | Browser PWA / local development |
|---|---|---|
| How you authenticate | header `X-Internal-Token: <INTERNAL_API_TOKEN>` on every request | `POST /api/auth/login` (form fields `email`, `password`), then the `JSESSIONID` cookie |
| CSRF token for POST / PUT / DELETE | not needed | needed: read it from `GET /api/auth/csrf` and send it in the header that answer names |
| When it applies | when the `INTERNAL_API_TOKEN` environment variable is set | when no token is configured |

- A missing or wrong token, or no session, answers **401** with the JSON error body below (never a redirect).
- A missing or expired CSRF token answers **403**; fetch a new one and retry.
- `POST /api/auth/login` answers 204 (a session starts) or 401; `POST /api/auth/logout` answers 204.
- Requests and answers are UTF-8 JSON. Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`, date-times ISO 8601. Money is a plain JSON number (euros).
- Lists are returned as plain JSON arrays, except `GET /api/recipes/search`: it is paged and answers `{items, total, page, pageSize, totalPages}` (24 per page unless `pageSize` says otherwise). `GET /api/recipes` still returns every recipe as a plain array.
- The service never decides for the user: it returns prices, savings and options, and the user chooses.

## Errors

Every error has the same shape:

```json
{ "status": 404, "error": "Not Found", "message": "No meal plan with id 99999" }
```

| Status | When |
|---|---|
| 400 | a missing or malformed parameter or body, an unknown diet preset, an invalid value |
| 401 | no valid token or session |
| 403 | missing or expired CSRF token |
| 404 | the id does not exist |
| 409 | the write conflicts with existing data (a foreign key, unique or primary key constraint) |
| 500 | anything else; the details are in the service log only |

#### POST /api/meal-plans/{id}/shopping-list

Builds and persists a shopping list from a plan's meals: one line per item still missing after
subtracting inventory, no store item pre-chosen. Returns the new list's id.

By default every planned meal is scaled by its own servings (the meal's own number, then its recipe's
preferred servings, then the household head count, then 2; see
ShoppingListService.generateFromMealPlanByServings), so a recipe planned twice counts twice. The
optional ?householdId=N lets the head count apply. An explicit ?people=N overrides all of
that: every recipe is scaled to N people, as before.

?shoppingDate=YYYY-MM-DD is the day of the shopping trip (default today, not in the past): the
offers that run on that day are the ones shown, so a list made today for a trip next week shows next week's
offers. ?from=YYYY-MM-DD is the first meal day the list counts (default the shopping day; pass the next
day when the shopping is after dinner). Every call makes a NEW list; earlier lists of the plan stay as they
were (GET /{id/shopping-lists} shows them). Stock is subtracted only in the same unit and only when it
has not expired by the shopping day; a unit mismatch leaves the line flagged needsReview.

**Path parameters**

| Name | Type |
|---|---|
| `id` | `int` |

**Query parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `people` | `Integer` | no |  |
| `householdId` | `Integer` | no |  |
| `shoppingDate` | `LocalDate` | no |  |
| `from` | `LocalDate` | no |  |



**Answer** 201 `GeneratedShoppingListDto`

```json
{
  "shoppingListId": 0
}
```

#### GET /api/meal-plans/{id}/shopping-lists

### PlannedMealController

The meal planner by date: read a week, plan a recipe on a day (as often as wanted), edit or move a planned meal,
remove it, and set a recipe's preferred servings. Every meal is addressed by its own entryId. A plan is
one Monday-to-Sunday week; the first meal added to a week creates its plan, so a page never has to create one.

The household is named with an optional householdId so the servings can follow its head count; the
PHP decides which household an account may use (see the backlog item "Auth and session review"). Without it,
a meal that has no number of its own and no recipe preference is cooked for 2.

### RecipeController


#### GET /api/recipes

All recipes by name. Optional diet rules, applied on the server (the client never filters 11,000 recipes):

- hard rules ("Was esse ich nicht?"): diet= (repeatable; halal, koscher, vegetarisch,
      vegan, see config/diet_presets.json; an unknown preset is a 400), excludeTags=a,b,
      excludeItems=;

- soft rules ("Was esse ich lieber nicht?"): avoidTags, avoidItems: recipes stay, are
      sorted after the others and list what matched in diet.softHits;

- includeUnclear=true|false (default false): recipes with a line that was not matched are
      UNCLEAR under a hard rule and left out unless this is true.

With rules every recipe carries diet (status OK / ANPASSBAR / UNCLEAR, hints, softHits); HIDDEN
recipes are not returned. The presets filter INGREDIENTS only; they are no halal or kosher certification:
meat certification stays the shopper's responsibility. Without any rule the answer is unchanged.
This is the plain list as an array; GET /api/recipes/search is the searchable, paged one.

**Query parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `diet` | `List<String>` | no |  |
| `excludeTags` | `List<String>` | no |  |
| `excludeItems` | `List<Integer>` | no |  |

#### GET /api/recipes/search

GET /api/recipes/search: search the recipes, one page of cards plus the total. Everything is applied
on the server (the client never filters 11,000 recipes). All filters are optional and combine with AND:

- search: q= (every word is in the recipe name), ingredient=a,b (repeatable; the
      recipe has an ingredient whose name contains each text);

- filters: tags=a,b (repeatable; the recipe carries all of these tags), minTime /
      maxTime (total time = prep + cook, minutes; recipes without a time are left out when either is
      set), servings=N (recipes for N people; a "3 – 4 Personen" recipe matches 3 and 4);

- order: sort=name|time|rating|newest (default name; ties always end by id, so the order is stable
      and paging neither repeats nor skips a recipe);

- paging: page (from 1, default 1) and pageSize (1 - 100, default 24). Without paging
      parameters you get the first 24 recipes, not all of them; use total / totalPages to go
      on. A page past the end is empty. Out-of-range values are a 400.

Optional diet rules, also applied on the server:

- hard rules ("Was esse ich nicht?"): diet= (repeatable; halal, koscher, vegetarisch,
      vegan, see config/diet_presets.json; an unknown preset is a 400), excludeTags=a,b,
      excludeItems=;

- soft rules ("Was esse ich lieber nicht?"): avoidTags, avoidItems: recipes stay, are
      sorted after the others and list what matched in diet.softHits;

- includeUnclear=true|false (default false): recipes with a line that was not matched are
      UNCLEAR under a hard rule and left out unless this is true.

With rules every card carries diet (status OK / ANPASSBAR / UNCLEAR, hints, softHits); HIDDEN recipes
are not returned and not counted in total. With rules the order is: no soft hit first, then OK before
ANPASSBAR before UNCLEAR, then the requested sort. The rules judge from a snapshot of the recipe facts that is
at most a minute old; GET /api/recipes/{id} always judges fresh. The presets filter INGREDIENTS only;
they are no halal or kosher certification: meat certification stays the shopper's responsibility.
GET /api/recipes is unchanged: the plain array of all recipes.

**Query parameters**

|---|---|---|---|
| `q` | `String` | no |  |
| `ingredient` | `List<String>` | no |  |
| `tags` | `List<String>` | no |  |
| `minTime` | `Integer` | no |  |
| `maxTime` | `Integer` | no |  |
| `servings` | `Integer` | no |  |
| `sort` | `String` | no |  |
| `page` | `Integer` | no |  |
| `pageSize` | `Integer` | no |  |
| `diet` | `List<String>` | no |  |
| `excludeTags` | `List<String>` | no |  |
| `excludeItems` | `List<Integer>` | no |  |
| `avoidTags` | `List<String>` | no |  |
| `avoidItems` | `List<Integer>` | no |  |
| `includeUnclear` | `boolean` | no | `false` |

A list parameter is repeated (`?diet=halal&diet=vegan`) or comma separated (`excludeTags=a,b`).

#### GET /api/recipes/{id}

The recipe with its ingredients and instructions. An optional ?people=N adds each
ingredient's quantity scaled by people / servings as scaledQuantity; the stored
quantity, the stored instruction text and the nutrition are never changed; each instruction's
scaledInstruction has its step amounts for people (a bracket always means 2 / 3 / 4 people;
otherwise the 2-person value scaled). An optional
?basis=max scales a "3 – 4 Personen" range recipe from its upper bound
(people / servingsMax) instead; it is ignored for a recipe that is not a range, and
?basis=servings is the default. The diet parameters of GET /api/recipes are accepted here
too: with any of them the answer carries diet with the same status and hints and the recipe's
unmatched ingredient lines (the recipe is returned even when its status is HIDDEN).

it only ranks and presents (see SuggestionService).

#### GET /api/suggestions/pantry

GET /api/suggestions/pantry: recipes that fit what the household has and what is on sale, one page of
suggestions plus the total. The purpose is healthy meals (all recipe data is cooked from fresh ingredients) at
the lowest shopping cost, so the default order best uses up the pantry first (ingredients that expire
soon weigh most), then needs the fewest ingredients bought at full price; pantry ingredients rank a recipe
higher, never lower. Every suggestion says which ingredients are in stock, which expire soon and which are
missing, and lists the offers on sale today for each missing one, every store, never one picked. All filters
are optional and combine with AND:

- q= (every word is in the recipe name), maxTime (total minutes at most; recipes
      without a time are left out), store= (a missing ingredient is on sale at that store);

- minMatches (ingredients in stock or on sale needed to show a recipe, default 1) and
      days (look-ahead for "expiring soon", default 7);

- sort=best|fewest-to-buy|expiring|name|time (default best; ties end by recipe id, so paging is
      stable);

- paging: page (from 1) and pageSize (1 - 100, default 24). Out-of-range values are a
      400.

The diet rules of GET /api/recipes/search apply here too, on the server: hard rules
(diet, excludeTags, excludeItems) hide a recipe the household does not eat and it is
not counted, soft rules (avoidTags, avoidItems) sort it after the others, and
includeUnclear (default false) lets recipes with an unmatched line through. With rules each recipe
card carries diet, and the order is: no soft hit first, then OK before ANPASSBAR before UNCLEAR, the
requested sort within each group.

The list holds at most 200 recipes, the best ones in the requested order (total is at most 200;
totalMatching says how many fit before the cap and capped whether it was cut); more are found
with GET /api/recipes/search.

An ingredient counts as in stock when the household has any of it and it has not expired; the amount is not
compared with the amount the recipe needs yet. Stock past its date is shown as EXPIRED and counts as
still to buy. This replaces the whole-list /by-savings for pages: that call is unchanged.

**Query parameters**

|---|---|---|---|
| `q` | `String` | no |  |
| `maxTime` | `Integer` | no |  |
| `store` | `String` | no |  |
| `minMatches` | `Integer` | no |  |
| `days` | `Integer` | no |  |
| `sort` | `String` | no |  |
| `page` | `Integer` | no |  |
| `pageSize` | `Integer` | no |  |
| `diet` | `List<String>` | no |  |
| `excludeTags` | `List<String>` | no |  |
| `excludeItems` | `List<Integer>` | no |  |
| `avoidTags` | `List<String>` | no |  |
| `avoidItems` | `List<Integer>` | no |  |
| `includeUnclear` | `boolean` | no | `false` |

A list parameter is repeated (`?diet=halal&diet=vegan`) or comma separated (`excludeTags=a,b`).

### DietDto

What the diet rules say about a recipe, present only when rules were passed.
status: OK, ANPASSBAR (excluded only through POSSIBLE animals of generic items: see hints),
UNCLEAR (a line of the recipe was not matched and a hard rule applies; only returned with includeUnclear) or
HIDDEN (excluded; returned only by GET /api/recipes/{id}, never in the list).
hints: per item that may come from an excluded animal, the animals it may still be (allowedAnimals,
e.g. Salami → Rind, Geflügel). softHits: what a soft rule (avoidTags / avoidItems) matched; absent when nothing.
unmatchedIngredients: the recipe's lines without a catalogue item (detail only).
Presets filter INGREDIENTS only; this is not a halal or kosher certification.

| Property | Type |
|---|---|
| `status` | `String` |
| `hints` | `List<Hint>` |
| `softHits` | `SoftHits` |
| `unmatchedIngredients` | `List<Unmatched>` |

### PantryIngredientDto

One ingredient of a suggested recipe. status is IN_STOCK, EXPIRING (in stock and expires

the recipe asks for (quantity null for "to taste"); stockQuantity / stockUnit is what the household
has, in the item's own unit; expiresOn is the earliest expiry date of the stock (null when unknown).

### PersistedShoppingListDto

A previously generated shopping list as it was persisted: its items with names, the amount still needed and its
unit, every current store option for each item (cheapest till price first, but not pre-picked) and the store item
the user has selected, if any. DAHÄM surfaces the options; it never chooses one for the user.

shoppingDate is the day of the trip the list was made for: the offers in the store options are the ones
that run on that day (validFrom / validUntil on each option say when). fromDate is the first
meal day the list counts. Both are null on a list made before they existed.

Each line: available is false when no store currently sells the item (the line is kept, never silently
dropped); needsReview is true when stock exists but in another unit than the line's, so nothing was
subtracted and a person checks it (stockQuantity / stockUnit show what the household has);
recipes are the recipes that need the line; purchased is the tick "bought" on the trip.

archived true = hidden from the overview (nothing is deleted); a free-text line (added with a name)
has no inventoryItemId, its text is in nameDeutsch and nameEnglish, and it has no store options.

status true = completed (read-only). storeTotals: for each store that sells something on the list,
how many of the lines still to buy it covers and what those lines cost there (the cheapest pack option per line);
shown side by side, never picked for the user.

| Property | Type |
|---|---|
| `id` | `int` |
| `mealPlanId` | `Integer` |
| `createdDate` | `LocalDate` |
| `shoppingDate` | `LocalDate` |
| `fromDate` | `LocalDate` |
| `status` | `boolean` |
| `archived` | `boolean` |
| `items` | `List<Line>` |
| `storeTotals` | `List<StoreTotal>` |

```json
{ … }
```

### RecipeCardDto

A recipe as a card in the list: what a card shows, nothing more (GET /api/recipes/{id} has the rest:
description, nutrition, image source, publish date, ingredients, instructions). totalTime is
prepTime + cookTime in minutes (0 when the recipe has no time). servings is the number of people;
servingsMax is the upper bound of a "3 – 4 Personen" range (servings is then the lower bound),
null otherwise. imageUrl / thumbnailUrl are links the browser loads from their source (null when
the recipe has no image: show a fallback; use the thumbnail in lists). cuisine is one German name,
ratingAvg is 0 - 5 with 2 decimals; both null when unknown. tags are the recipe's tag names (no
group or source: the detail has those), sorted by group then name; empty when it has none.
diet is present only when diet rules were passed to GET /api/recipes (see DietDto).

| Property | Type |
|---|---|

| `thumbnailUrl` | `String` |
| `prepTime` | `int` |

| `cuisine` | `String` |

### RecipeDetailDto

One recipe with its nutrition, ingredients and ordered instructions, as returned by /api/recipes/{id}.
servingsMax is the upper bound of a "3 – 4 Personen" range (servings is then the
lower bound), null when the recipe is not a range. people is the head count asked for with
?people=N (null when not asked); each ingredient's scaledQuantity is its
quantity scaled to that count, from servings by default or from servingsMax
when basis is "max", and each instruction's scaledInstruction is its step text
with the amounts for that count. basis is the one actually used: "max" only when
it was asked for and the recipe is a range. scalable is false when that servings count is
not positive, in which case nothing is scaled. The enrichment fields (description,
imageUrl, thumbnailUrl, imageSource, cuisine, ratingAvg,
ratingCount, publishedDate) are as in RecipeSummaryDto; null when missing. tags are the recipe's tags, sorted by group then name:
source is "manual" (added by a person) or "derived" (worked out from DAHÄM's data).
diet is present only when diet rules were passed (see DietDto): the status, the hints and the
recipe's unmatched ingredient lines.

| `cookTime` | `int` |

| `thumbnailUrl` | `String` |

| `publishedDate` | `LocalDate` |
